newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Spain must free telecoms sector, EU says.
newsitem.headline: Spain must free telecoms sector, EU says.

text.p: The European Commission, under pressure to make a fresh offer on WTO telecoms talks in Geneva, has told the Spanish government that it must liberalise its telecommunications sector from the first half of 1998 by granting licences.

In a letter to the Spanish government, European Commissioner Karel Van Miert asked Madrid to give quick confirmation that it is adhering to the January 1, 1998 deadline for the full liberalisation of telecoms services and infrastructure in the European Union.
He also insisted that Madrid commit itself to grant licences to new telecoms operators during ythe first half od 1998.
The issue of telecoms liberalisation holds the key to the Commission's clearance of a joint venture between four European operators including Telefonica de Espana SA and AT & T.

The Commission is also under pressure from the U.S. government in the Geneva talks to ensure that all major European telecoms markets are effectively opened to free competition from the agreed 1998 deadline. Spain is the fifth biggest telecoms market in the EU.
